# Form

## Use when
- The user enters or edits values that are submitted together (sign-up, profile, payment details, one onboarding step).
- A sequence of steps collects related values and carries progress (use the flow shell for the steps, this pattern for each step's fields).

## Don't use when
- Each control applies the moment it changes. That is the Settings pattern (Switch rows), not a form with a Save button.
- The screen is read-only. Show values as text, not disabled inputs.
- The only input is one search box. Use Input alone, no Label row or Submit.

## Decision rules
- Text, email, number, password, search → `Input`. Multi-line → `Textarea`.
- One of 2–6 options, all visible → `RadioGroup`. One of more than 5, or a long list → `Select`. Never a raw `<select>` or radio input.
- Value submitted later with the form → `Checkbox`. Applies instantly → `Switch`, and then it is not part of this form.
- Every field has a `Label` with `htmlFor` equal to the control's `id`. Required fields set `required` on the Label (never a typed asterisk); optional fields in a mostly-required form set `optional`. Never rely on the placeholder as the label.
- Validation error on a field → set `invalid` on the control and render the message in text wired with `aria-describedby`. Never use an `Alert` per field error.
- A form-level failure (submit failed, server rejected) → one `Alert` `variant="danger"` above the actions. For its recovery wording see the Error recovery pattern.
- Validate on blur for format, on submit for required. Do not show errors before the user has touched a field, except after a failed submit.
- Keep Submit enabled and validate on press, so the user is told what is wrong. Show `loading` on the Button while submitting. Disable Submit only when the amount or choice that makes it meaningful is missing (for example an amount flow's Continue).
- Skippable optional step → a `Button variant="ghost"` "Skip" beside the primary action, not a link.

## Components and variants
- `Label` variant: `default` · size: `md`
- `Input` variant: `default` · size: `md`
- `Select` size: `md`
- `RadioGroup` variant: `default` · size: `md`
- `Checkbox` variant: `default` · size: `md`
- `Button` variant: `primary`, `ghost` · size: `md`
- `Alert` variant: `danger` · size: `md`

## Layout and density
- One column. Fields stack with the spacing token `--atlas-spacing-4` between field groups and `--atlas-spacing-1_5` between a Label and its control.
- Primary action last, full width on a phone, `primary` once per view. Secondary actions (Back, Skip) use `ghost`.
- Match control size to Label size (`md` with `md`). Use `lg` only on touch-first screens.

## Hierarchy and composition
- Order: step title and one line of help → fields → form-level Alert (when present) → actions.
- Group related fields in a `Card variant="outlined"` only when the screen has more than one group. A single group sits directly on the page.
- Do not nest Cards.

## Responsive behavior
- Phone: one column, actions pinned below the fields. Wider than the tablet breakpoint: keep one column up to the content width token; put short paired fields (expiry and CVC) side by side only.

## States
- default · focus (component focus ring, never removed) · invalid · disabled · loading (Button `loading`, fields not disabled individually unless submission locks them).
- loading: while submitting, keep entered values visible.
- empty: an empty required field shows its error after a submit attempt.
- error: field error in text, form-level failure in one Alert.

## Accessibility
- Every control is named (Label or `aria-label`). Error text is referenced with `aria-describedby`.
- On a failed submit, move focus to the first invalid field.
- Do not use placeholder text as the only instruction. Keep Enter-to-submit working (use a real `<form>`).

## Anti-patterns
- Typed "*" in a label instead of `required`.
- Disabled input to show read-only data.
- An Alert for every field error, or an error shown only by red colour.
- Switch inside a form that also has Save for the same value.
- Hand-rolled `<input>`, `<select>` or radio inputs.

## Example
```tsx
import * as React from "react"
import { Alert } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/Alert/Alert"
import { Button } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Button/Button"
import { Input } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Input/Input"
import { Label } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Label/Label"

type Errors = { name?: string; email?: string }

export function ProfileForm({ onSave }: { onSave: (v: { name: string; email: string }) => Promise<void> }) {
  const [name, setName] = React.useState("")
  const [email, setEmail] = React.useState("")
  const [errors, setErrors] = React.useState<Errors>({})
  const [failed, setFailed] = React.useState(false)
  const [saving, setSaving] = React.useState(false)

  async function submit(e: React.FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault()
    const next: Errors = {}
    if (!name.trim()) next.name = "Enter your full name."
    if (!/^\S+@\S+\.\S+$/.test(email)) next.email = "Enter a valid email address."
    setErrors(next)
    if (next.name || next.email) return
    setSaving(true)
    setFailed(false)
    try {
      await onSave({ name, email })
    } catch {
      setFailed(true)
    } finally {
      setSaving(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={submit} noValidate style={{ display: "grid", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-4)" }}>
      <div>
        <Label htmlFor="name" required>Full name</Label>
        <Input id="name" value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)}
          invalid={!!errors.name} aria-describedby={errors.name ? "name-error" : undefined} />
        {errors.name && <p id="name-error" style={{ color: "var(--atlas-danger)" }}>{errors.name}</p>}
      </div>
      <div>
        <Label htmlFor="email" required>Email</Label>
        <Input id="email" type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
          invalid={!!errors.email} aria-describedby={errors.email ? "email-error" : undefined} />
        {errors.email && <p id="email-error" style={{ color: "var(--atlas-danger)" }}>{errors.email}</p>}
      </div>
      {failed && <Alert variant="danger" title="We couldn't save your details" description="Your entries are still here. Check your connection and try again." />}
      <Button type="submit" variant="primary" loading={saving}>Save</Button>
    </form>
  )
}
```
